speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn presenting with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting; to begin my assessment, how many days old are you, and was your birth vaginal or Cesarean?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Malrotation with Midgut Volvulus. The clinical presentation of bilious vomiting in a newborn born at term is a surgical emergency until proven otherwise, and the strong family history of pyloric stenosis does not explain the immediate onset of bilious vomiting which is characteristic of intestinal obstruction at the level of the duodenum or proximal jejunum. Immediate surgical consultation and an abdominal X-ray are required.
